title: Adaptive Prefix Economizer: hit-curve emulator, budget-aware TTL laddering, and safe apply protocol
creator: Alice Chen
description:
Background:
Redwood's KV/prefix cache tuning currently relies on static heuristics and ad-hoc rollouts. Teams are spending engineering time hand-tuning TTLs and cache key shapes, and cost regressions occur when cache policies are misapplied to different traffic mixes. We need automation that: models hit-rate sensitivity to prefix key design and TTL ladders, recommends budget-aware changes, and applies them with a safe, observable rollout protocol that supports quick rollback.

Goal:
1) Build a hit-curve emulator that predicts per-prefix hit-rate and token-cost impact under TTL and keying changes using historical traces and efficient counterfactual sampling.
2) Provide budget-aware TTL ladder suggestions (e.g., per-prefix TTL bands and prefetch/hedging knobs) that balance latency SLOs and token spend.
3) Implement a safe apply/rollback protocol with deterministic canary fencing, automated impact checks, and staged rollback triggers.

Success criteria (measurable):
- Simulator MAPE <= 8% for prefix hit-rate predictions across 90% of high-volume prefixes.
- Average token spend reduction of 6-12% on targeted workloads when applying recommendations in pilot before model/quantization changes.
- No customer-facing latency SLO violations attributable to rollout (customer_impact: none).
- Automated rollback completes within 3 minutes of trigger for staged deploys.

Scope:
- Data ingestion: prefix access logs, per-request keys, model sequence length distribution, route/model metadata, per-token cost estimates.
- Modeling: lightweight hit-curve emulator (parametric fit + small NN residual) that runs on sampled traces.
- Recommendations: TTL ladder (tiered TTLs per prefix population), suggested key canonicalization rules (affix stripping, length bucketing), and prefetch/hedging knobs.
- Orchestration: safe apply lib used by runtime rollout controller supporting dry-run, canary fences, staged percentage ramp, automated impact tests, and rollback.

Approach / Design Notes:
1) Hit-curve emulator:
   - Fit per-prefix cacheability curves using an interpretable parametric base (e.g., double-exponential or Weibull), with a small residual model to capture burstiness and seasonality.
   - Use stratified sampling by prefix volume and sequence length to keep training and inference fast.
   - Expose uncertainty bands for each prediction so the rollout controller can make risk-aware decisions.

2) TTL ladder generator (budget-aware):
   - Input: budget delta target (tokens/month or cost/month) and SLO guardrails.
   - Output: TTL bands (e.g., hot/warmer/cold) and a per-band prefetch/hedge policy.
   - Heuristic: raise TTL on high-stability prefixes, reduce on low-stability prefixes, but always ensure a min TTL for tail latency-sensitive routes.

3) Cache key design recommendations:
   - Produce canonicalization rules (strip low-value query params, normalize timestamps to granularity buckets, collapse high-cardinality suffixes).
   - Score candidate key rules by expected hit uplift vs. expected false-positive conflation risk.

4) Safe apply and rollback protocol:
   - Dry-run mode: compute predicted impact on live traces without changing runtime state.
   - Canary fences: select risk-diverse set of hosts and customer routes to isolate variance.
   - Staged ramp with automated statistical tests: check hit-rate delta, token spend, P95 latency, and error rates at each step.
   - Rollback triggers: breach of SLO guardrails, prediction mismatch beyond uncertainty band, or increase in errors.
   - Rollback path must be deterministic, idempotent, and observable in Console with links to failing metrics.

Data & Telemetry Requirements:
- 7-day rolling prefix access histogram (per-prefix counts, unique keys, avg seq length).
- Per-request annotation for TTL and keying policy during dry-run.
- Cost attribution pipeline (tokens attributed to prefixed groups).
- Tracing hooks to correlate cache hits/misses to downstream latency.

Milestones:
- M1 (2w): Data pipeline + sampled trace extractor and schema.
- M2 (3w): Hit-curve emulator prototype + unit tests and offline evaluation harness.
- M3 (3w): TTL ladder generator + recommendations UI spec.
- M4 (2w): Safe apply library + canary fencing integration with rollout controller.
- M5 (2w): End-to-end pilot on two internal routes, dashboards, and failover drills.

Rollout Plan (pilot -> staged):
- Pilot: internal routes for Console and SDK logging (low customer exposure), manual approval.
- Stage 1: 5% traffic across non-SLAbound routes for 48h with automated checks.
- Stage 2: 25% traffic for 72h; longer observation windows.
- Stage 3: 100% for targeted tenant segment with extended observation and manual signoff for broad rollout.

Observability + Alerts:
- Dashboards: per-prefix predicted vs actual hit-rate, token-spend delta, P95 generation latency, canary host deltas.
- Alerts: automatic if predicted vs actual hit-rate drift > 12% across any canary for 15m, or token spend > budget threshold.

Testing Strategy:
- Unit tests for emulator components and canonicalization rules.
- Integration tests against replayed traces and a synthetic workload generator that can simulate prefix bursts and seasonal patterns.
- Chaos exercises: force canary host failure and validate rollback.

Security & Compliance:
- Ensure dry-run traces are sanitized and PII removed before training.
- security_review_required: true

Open questions / Risks:
- Q1: How to select risk-diverse canary set automatically? (Options: stratify by tenant size, route volume, and region).
- Q2: Model drift detection sensitivity — need to tune uncertainty bands to avoid excessive rollbacks.
- Risk: Over-canonicalization can increase erroneous conflation leading to quality regressions; must include manual review for high-risk rules.

Links / Artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Adaptive+Prefix+Economizer+Design
- Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8234
- Simulation notebooks: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/kv-hit-emulator-simulations

Next steps:
- Curate a list of 200 high-volume prefixes for early evaluation.
- Run M1 data pipeline, hand-validate 10 prefixes against simulator to calibrate.
- Schedule two-hour rollout tabletop with SRE/Runtime/Console owners for M4 handoff.
